$comment: Transaction-boundary signatures, owned by the harness -- never read from the
candidate's own nfr-trace.json. Used ONLY to build the TXN_BOUNDARY edge in the code
graph: a function that opens a transaction scope is linked to every function called
This is deliberately NOT a full per-tactic mechanism table. Scoring how strongly a
function implements a tactic (E_call inside S(x,f)) belongs to the binding provider,
not to TICS -- see validators/tics/contract.py. Keeping the two tables separate stops
the same ground truth from being owned in two places.
Patterns match the dotted attribute path of the call target. '*' matches one receiver
segment, so '*.begin' matches session.begin() and self._session.begin() alike.

context_managers.note: asyncpg/psycopg connection.transaction, and the widespread unit-of-work convention uow.transaction()
django-style atomic() bound to another name

calls.note: explicit commit closes a transaction scope
explicit rollback closes a transaction scope

known_false_positives: '*.transaction' is broad on purpose. It is what catches the unit-of-work pattern, which
is the dominant way transaction boundaries appear in generated FastAPI/SQLAlchemy code,
but it will also match an unrelated attribute called .transaction. Every TXN_BOUNDARY
edge is emitted with the matched pattern attached so a false positive is auditable in
the report rather than silently inflating a score.
